ai.definition: Mixture of Experts (MoE) is a neural network architecture designed to enhance the efficiency and scalability of large language models (LLMs) by selectively activating only a subset of parameters for each input.
ai.howItWorks: In MoE, a gating network evaluates each token in an input sequence and routes it to one or more 'expert' sub-networks. This routing is based on the relevance of the expert to the current token, ensuring that only necessary computations are performed, thus reducing overall compute cost per token.
ai.problemSolved: MoE addresses the challenge of scaling large neural networks by reducing computational overhead and resource requirements while maintaining or even improving model performance.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process for MoE involves designing and training the gating network along with the expert sub-networks. This requires significant computational resources, particularly during the initial training phase when optimizing the routing mechanism.
ai.buildProcess: The build process starts by defining the architecture of the expert sub-networks, followed by the design of the gating network. Training involves both fine-tuning the experts and optimizing the gating function to ensure efficient token routing.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the complexity of training the gating mechanism, the number of expert sub-networks required, and the computational resources needed for inference when only a subset of parameters is active.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: MoE is expected to continue evolving as more applications emerge, with potential improvements in efficiency and performance driving broader adoption.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory landscape does not specifically address MoE, but compliance with general data protection regulations will be necessary for any implementation involving user data.
ai.risks: Risks include the complexity of designing an effective gating mechanism, potential degradation in model performance if routing is suboptimal, and challenges in scaling the architecture to handle large datasets efficiently.
ai.profitability: Profitability depends on the specific application and market conditions. While MoE can reduce operational costs, its adoption rate will impact overall profitability.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may focus on improving the gating mechanism's accuracy, optimizing expert sub-networks for different tasks, and exploring hybrid architectures that combine MoE with other techniques like quantization or pruning.

glossary.def: A neural network architecture where a gating mechanism routes input tokens to relevant expert sub-networks, reducing computational overhead.
The component in MoE that evaluates each token and decides which expert sub-network(s) it should be routed to based on its relevance.
Specialized neural network components within the MoE architecture designed to handle specific types of input tokens efficiently.

subsystems.name: Expert networks
subsystems.role: independent feed-forward sub-networks that specialise in different patterns or token types.

subsystems.name: Router (gating network)
subsystems.role: scores each token and decides which experts should process it.

subsystems.name: Token dispatch and combine
subsystems.role: sends tokens to the chosen experts and merges their outputs into one representation.

subsystems.name: Load balancing
subsystems.role: keeps experts from collapsing to a few favourites, so all get trained.

subsystems.name: Distributed execution
subsystems.role: spreads experts across many accelerators and keeps them fed with tokens.

subsystems.name: Training system
subsystems.role: backpropagates through sparse routing and updates every expert and the router.

buildSteps.title: Choose the transformer backbone
buildSteps.detail: Decide the number of layers, attention heads, and hidden size; attention and residual connections stay dense and shared across all tokens.

buildSteps.title: Define the expert layers
buildSteps.detail: Replace each dense feed-forward block with a set of several expert feed-forward networks (for example, 8 or more), each with the same input and output dimensions.

buildSteps.title: Add the router
buildSteps.detail: Attach a small linear layer to every MoE layer that produces a score for each expert for every token.

buildSteps.title: Implement top-k routing
buildSteps.detail: For each token, select the k highest-scoring experts (often k=1 or 2), normalise their gate values, and discard the rest.

buildSteps.title: Add a load-balancing loss
buildSteps.detail: Include an auxiliary loss that encourages the router to spread tokens evenly, preventing a few experts from being overused while others are starved.

buildSteps.title: Distribute experts
buildSteps.detail: Shard experts across devices using expert parallelism; tokens are sent to the relevant device via all-to-all communication and results are returned.

buildSteps.title: Train the model
buildSteps.detail: Run forward and backward passes; gradients flow to the router and the selected experts. Use a capacity factor to cap how many tokens an expert may process per batch.

buildSteps.title: Fine-tune and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Convert the trained model to inference-optimised kernels, fuse operations, and serve it with expert caching to reduce communication overhead.

prerequisites.why: MoE replaces parts of a transformer; the attention and residual structure is needed for the token representations that the experts process.
experts are spread across many accelerators, so training requires fast interconnects and efficient gradient synchronisation.
top-k routing and load-balancing methods are well-studied and used in production models.
tokens must be shuffled between devices frequently, so low-latency, high-bandwidth communication is essential.
MoE trades memory capacity for compute, so it needs many devices to hold all experts and their parameters.

pathway.milestone: MoE used in frontier large language models to scale parameter count without proportional compute per token
pathway.unlocks: larger, more capable models that remain affordable to run at inference time.

pathway.milestone: finer-grained experts and improved routing such as expert-choice or adaptive top-k
pathway.unlocks: better quality per parameter and more stable training with less token dropping.

pathway.milestone: MoE applied to multimodal models and on-device inference with expert offloading
pathway.unlocks: efficient on-device AI and models that can reason across text, images and audio.

pathway.milestone: adaptive computation where the model learns to allocate more experts to harder inputs
pathway.unlocks: dynamic efficiency and potentially stronger reasoning by spending compute only where needed.
